chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Fadhl, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Muawiya ibn Sharih, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the Imam breaks his ritual purity while he is in prayer, it is not appropriate for anyone to advance except the one who witnessed the Iqamah. When the Mu'adhdhin says 'The prayer has stood', it is appropriate for those in the mosque to stand on their feet and advance some of themselves, and not wait for the Imam.' I said: 'And if the Imam is the Mu'adhdhin?' He said: 'And if he is, they should not wait for him and should advance some of themselves.'

This is not contradictory to what we have presented, because in his saying (peace be upon him) 'It is not appropriate for anyone to advance except the one who witnessed the Iqamah', there is not a prohibition against the advancement of the one who did not witness it in the sense of strict forbiddance, but it is explicit that it is the preferred and superior act. For if the meaning were prohibition, the wording of the prohibition or the removal of permissibility for that action would have been included. Whenever this is not mentioned, we know that he meant the superior act. And if there were wording of prohibition, we would interpret it as referring to the superior act based on the indication of the preceding narrations. And that which he narrated:

key_terms.الْإِقَامَةَ: the Iqamah (call to prayer signaling the start)

ai.seo_question: What should the congregation do if the Imam breaks his ritual purity during prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of immediate succession in congregational prayer when the Imam experiences minor impurity, emphasizing that the congregation should not wait but rather advance among themselves based on merit. The commentary clarifies that the instruction is one of preference (*afdalah*) rather than strict prohibition (*hazr*), ensuring the continuity of the prayer without delay. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the fluidity of leadership within the prayer unit to maintain its validity and spiritual integrity.
